meta.mode_reason: Rich verified real imagery -> photographic (the primary mode). The Designer's cinematic_background_pool registers 6 license-clean, >=1280px landscape cover-ables (des_01 Mindelo harbour, sct_04 Hard Rock aerial, sct_05 Delfshaven, sct_06 Ernestina under sail, sct_07 Praia, sct_03 Rotterdam WC flags) — at the 5-floor with one to spare, for a place/people/sport story whose geography (Miami / Rotterdam / the islands / the sea) IS the argument. No generative or data_driven fallback is needed or allowed to displace real photos.
meta.gradient_scene_decision: ZERO kind:color|gradient scenes, deliberately. The dense-interactive sections (edt_02 odds explorer, edt_05 scrolly map, edt_09 double scrolly) do NOT get gradient interludes — validate.py Section 6c hard-errors ANY gradient/color scene in photographic mode (cin_photographic_gradient_rest, the PIT-54 black-scroll-gap bug). Instead those beats HOLD the adjacent real photo rendered framed (blurred-darkened cover fill) under a near-opaque scrim, so the photographic surface quiets to near-silence without ever going black or fighting the charts.

global.engine: One pinned full-bleed .cin-stage (position:fixed, inset:0, z-index behind <main>) holding one .cin-bg layer per scene, stacked. The ACTIVE layer has opacity 1, all others 0; scene switching is an IntersectionObserver on the section beats (data-backs=teaser|edt_xx; rootMargin '-45% 0px -45% 0px', threshold 0 — the beat whose middle crosses the viewport middle activates its layer) toggling an .active class; the crossfade is a CSS transition:opacity 1.15s ease (NEVER a JS tween, NEVER a forced-reflow restart like void el.offsetWidth). Text scrolls over the stage in <main> with per-scene scrims painted inside each .cin-bg plus the body backplate below. Copy the working reference build (cinematographer/references/example_cinematic_scroll.html) for the exact CSS/JS, restyled to THIS page's tokens (bg #0A1420, ink #EAE6DC, accent #F2B544) — not the example's mint.
global.reduced_motion: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce): no crossfade, no ken-burns, no parallax, no hero video (cin_00 -> poster assets/teaser.jpg; the .teaser overlay stays static and fully opaque). Each section paints its scene's image as a STATIC scrimmed per-section background (the framed holds keep their blur+dim grade as static CSS). The page reads fully with motion off; JS-off degrades the same way (per-section static backgrounds; never a bare or white column).
global.performance: Lazy-decode: every .cin-bg gets decoding='async' + img.decode() on preload; only the current and next scene's images are decoded/upgraded (IO with a generous rootMargin marks 'near' scenes); crossfade current+next pair only, will-change:opacity ONLY on that pair (remove after transition). All grade filters (blur/brightness/grayscale) are STATIC per layer — never animated at scroll-time. Parallax + the hero overlay dissolve run in one rAF-throttled scroll handler, transform/opacity only, parallax capped +-6vh. The framed holds re-use the SAME image file as their sharp sibling (browser cache — zero extra bytes: 6 photos + 1 video cover 11 scenes). Total background weight ~1.5 MB images + the 8s teaser loop. Mobile <=700px: parallax OFF, ken-burns OFF, crossfade kept; the sticky stage uses 100svh; hero prefers the mp4 (small loop) with poster-first paint, poster-only under Save-Data.
global.interaction_coexistence: The cinematic IO watches ONLY section-level beats (the teaser + the ten data-edt sections) — never the .step divs inside int_03/int_04/int_06/int_09, which run their OWN sticky+IO engines (rootMargin '-40% 0 -40% 0') for step logic. One scene per section means the background NEVER changes mid-scrolly; it holds while a scrolly's interior steps fire. Stacking: .cin-stage lowest; scrolly sticky panels, widgets, charts and the frosted plates live in <main>'s stacking context above it. The scrollies' sticky graphics carry their own opaque panel surfaces (--surface #101D2B family) so their SVGs never depend on the background for contrast.
global.readability: Two-tier legibility, per cinematic_recipes.readability_scrims: (1) per-scene scrims as specced on each cin_xx (bottom-anchored, tuned darker for evidence/interactive-heavy beats); (2) a frosted dark BACKPLATE on the prose sections — main>section:not(.teaser):not(.refs){ background:rgba(10,20,32,.6); backdrop-filter:blur(3px); -webkit-backdrop-filter:blur(3px) } — at the PROSE width: wide charts/maps/card-decks break out as their own frosted figures, but data-grid tables stay WITHIN the backplate measure (tables-vs-charts split, PIT-67). Text-shadow alone is never relied on. All chart guide text stays in --ink/--muted light values (dark-mode-safe gate).
global.continuity: Connective thread = the star-gold accent (#F2B544): the 1px scroll-progress hairline on the stage, scene credits and the kicker rules all use it, and every background is graded toward the deep-Atlantic navy (#0A1420 family) so no scene jumps palette — the one deliberate tonal event is the cin_07 (grey, darkest) -> cin_08 (daylight) recovery, which is the story's own emotional turn. Geography arcs Mindelo -> Miami -> Rotterdam -> the sea -> Mindelo (dark) -> Praia -> Rotterdam (flags): the page opens on the islands and closes on the diaspora, which is the thesis.
global.credits: Each scene's credit renders small (bottom-right of the stage, --muted, 11-12px) from the media_ref's verified attribution_text, switching with the active scene; cin_00's credit lives on the .teaser overlay per hero.json. CC BY-SA / CC BY attributions verbatim as specced per scene; the NPS public-domain line kept for sct_06.
global.tagging: The Programmer tags every layer data-cin='cin_xx' + data-des/data-sct from its media_ref (cin_00 -> data-des='des_01'; the .teaser overlay separately carries data-des='des_hero_video' as the hero's Verify hit). All ids resolve against scout.json/designer.json registries (validate.py Section 6).
